headlines.text: Flash back to 2019, when Chris Jericho vs. Cody clashed for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Full Gear, rated 8.20 ? an excellent showing. For Cody, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. A defining moment in AEW's early history ? Cody's best friend MJF threw in the towel to end the match, then kicked Cody in the groin as a full-on heel turn, a moment that got over huge with the live crowd chanting in disbelief.
That Wednesday in 2022, The Gunn Club left that name behind for good, stepping out as The Gunns after 11 matches under the old identity, on Dynamite.

Rewind to 2024, when Castagnoli, PAC & Yuta vs. Briscoe, Ishii & O'Reilly went to battle over the AEW World Trios Titles, appearing on Collision, rated 6.87. For Briscoe, Ishii & O'Reilly, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. Championship gold always raises the stakes.

secondaries.text: On this day in 2019, Jon Moxley vs. Kenny Omega fought it out in a Lights Out match, in the show-closing main event slot on Full Gear, rated 8.96 ? a genuine showstealer in a hard-fought men's division clash ? part of a stacked Full Gear '19 card, rated 8.06 overall. An unsanctioned, nearly 40-minute war of pure violence ? barbed wire bats, broken glass, and mousetraps all came into play before Moxley finally put Omega away, in a match still remembered as one of the most brutal in AEW's history.
That Saturday in 2019, Proud-N-Powerful touched down in AEW for the first time as a team, appearing on Full Gear, rated 7.45 ? a solid showing.

On a Wednesday in 2022, back when Bryan Danielson vs. Sammy Guevara settled things in a 2 out of 3 Falls match, closing out the card as the main event on Dynamite, rated 7.83 ? a good, competitive contest.
